title: Euclidean Geometry: Proportionality and Similar Triangles
seo_title: Grade 12 Proportionality and Similarity Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Revise earlier work on the necessary and sufficient conditions for polygons to be similar; prove (accepting results established in earlier grades): that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally (and the midpoint theorem as a special case); that equiangular triangles are similar; that triangles with sides in proportion are similar; the Pythagorean theorem by similar triangles.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 Euclidean geometry worksheets: the proportionality theorem, similar triangles, ratios of sides and areas. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Proportionality theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
  • Equiangular triangles are similar, and their corresponding sides are in proportion.
  • Match the sides opposite equal angles.
  • If the sides are in the ratio k, the areas are in the ratio k².

Examples

Example

DE ∥ BC, AD = 4, DB = 6, AE = 6

4/6 = 6/EC

Answer: EC = 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong sidesMatch sides opposite equal angles.
AD : DBDE : BC = AD : AB.
AreasSquare the ratio.

items.q: In △ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC with DE ∥ BC. AD = 2 cm, DB = 5 cm and AE = 4 cm. Find EC.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 61° and 69°. △DEF has angles of 61° and 75°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: Only one pair of angles matches (61°). The other angles of △DEF are 75° and 44°, not 69° and 50°. No.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 73° and 71°. △DEF has angles of 71° and 36°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The third angle of △ABC is 36°, so both triangles have angles 73°, 71° and 36°. Two pairs of congruent angles: Yes, by AA similarity.

items.q: △ABC has sides 6, 7 and 9. △DEF has sides 18, 21 and 28. Are the triangles similar?

items.e: AB : DE and AC : DF are both 1 : 3, and the included angles are congruent. Yes, by SAS similarity.

items.q: CD is the altitude to the hypotenuse. AD = 4 and DB = 16. Find CD.
items.e: The altitude is the geometric mean of the two segments: CD² = AD × DB = 4 × 16 = 64, so CD = 8.
